steps: Click the More button (⋮) at the top right of the side panel, then click Extension settings to open the Options page.
Click Options in the left list, find the Appearance section and the Theme select.
Choose Light, then Dark, then System, and go back to the side panel after each choice.
Compare the page background and panel backgrounds in each theme: each should change as a whole with no leftover fixed colours.
S6.01.where: Page and panel backgrounds across the whole side panel; they change when the theme changes under Extension settings > Options > Theme

S6.02.note: The code sets the menu surface through the shared tokens; the exact elevation was not measured.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button at the top right of the side panel.
Look at the menu panel against the chat background behind it.
Switch the theme to Light and then Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and open More again.
Compare: the menu should look raised above the page in both themes, as a separate surface.
S6.02.where: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header; the menu is the raised surface

S6.03.needs: a chat reply (signed-in account not verified in code)
S6.03.note: A 4.5:1 contrast ratio needs a colour meter; the tester can only check readability by eye.
steps: Send any message in the chat and wait for a reply.
Read the reply text and the small muted row under the message.
Switch the theme to Light and then Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and look again.
Compare: primary and muted text should both stay readable on the panel background in both themes.
S6.03.where: Reply text and muted caption text in the chat, such as the small row under a message

steps: Click the More (⋮) button and look at the edge of the menu.
Look at the edge of the message box at the bottom of the side panel.
Switch the theme to Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and look at both edges again.
Compare: both borders should be visible but subtle, in both themes.
S6.04.where: The border around the message box at the bottom of the chat and the border of the More menu

S6.05.note: The on-fill and text roles were read in the code, not measured.
steps: Drag across a line of reply text to select it and look at the selection highlight.
Look at the accent-tinted model selector button in the chat header.
Switch the theme to Light and then Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and repeat.
Compare: the selection and accent colours should stay readable with the text on them in both themes.
S6.05.where: Accent colour on the model selector button in the chat header, and the text selection highlight in a reply

S6.06.needs: a way to make a copy or save fail (not found in code)
S6.06.note: Triggering a real failure was not confirmed, and status colours for success, warning and info were not checked on screen.
steps: Find a place where the panel shows a failure notice, such as a failed copy of a message.
Read the notice text and check that it is readable on its background.
Switch the theme to Dark under Extension settings > Options > Theme and look at the notice again.
Compare: error and status text should stay readable in both themes.
S6.06.where: Warning or error text in the panel, for example the copy failure message

S6.07.note: The editorial family was not confirmed on screen; the code declares UI and monospace families in side_panel.ts.
steps: Send a message and read the reply text in the chat.
Find a code block in a reply, or ask for one.
Compare the sans-serif text with the monospace code text.
Compare: the UI font, the editorial font and the monospace font should each look like one declared family.
S6.07.where: Font faces in chat text, headings and code blocks

S6.08.note: Whether a reply returns headings depends on the model, and the sizes were read from tokens, not measured.
steps: Ask the chat for an answer with a heading, a sub-heading and a small heading.
Look at the three heading levels in the reply.
Compare: each level should have a clear step in size and weight, the same across replies.

S6.09.note: No in-app text-size control was found in apps/extension/src; respect for the OS text-size setting was not confirmed.
steps: Send a message and read the reply body text.
Compare the body text with the smaller caption text under a message.
Compare: body text should use one base size across replies.
S6.09.where: Body text in the chat and in the menus

S6.10.note: The caption token resolves to 14px in side_panel.css, which is the small body size, not a 12px role.
steps: Send a message and find the small row under the reply.
Read the caption text and compare its size with the body text.
Compare: captions should stay readable and not smaller than the small text size set in the tokens.
S6.10.where: Caption and metadata text, such as the small row under a chat message

steps: Ask the chat for a short code sample and wait for the reply.
Compare the code text with the body text next to it.
Compare: code should use a monospace font and a size of its own.
S6.11.where: Code blocks and inline code in a chat reply

steps: Send a message that gets a multi-line reply with a heading and a code block.
Compare the line spacing of body text, heading and code.
Compare: each text role should have its own line spacing that suits its size.
S6.12.where: Line spacing in multi-line replies, headings, body and code

S6.13.needs: a chat reply with several paragraphs
steps: Ask the chat for an answer with at least three paragraphs.
Look at the gap between the paragraphs.
Compare: the gap should be the same between every pair of paragraphs.
S6.13.where: Gap between paragraphs in a reply

S6.14.needs: a chat reply with a list
S6.14.note: The list indent rule was read only by its line number in side_panel.ts.
steps: Ask the chat for a list with a nested sub-list.
Look at the indent of the top list and the nested list.
Compare: each nested level should step in by the same amount.
S6.14.where: Indent of bulleted and numbered lists in a reply, and nested lists

steps: Ask the chat for a code block.
Look at the space between the code text and the edge of the code box on all sides.
Compare: the padding should look the same on every side.
S6.15.where: Padding inside code blocks in a reply

S6.16.needs: a chat reply with a table
steps: Ask the chat for a small table with a header row.
Look at the padding in each table cell.
Compare: all cells should have the same padding and the table should not overflow the panel.
S6.16.where: Cells of a table in a reply

steps: Send two messages in a row and wait for both replies.
Look at the space between each message and the next one.
Compare: the space between turns should be the same each time.
S6.17.where: Space between one chat turn and the next

S6.18.note: The action row is shown inside the message bubble; whether it appears only on hover was not confirmed.
steps: Send a message and wait for a reply.
Look at the row directly under your message and under the reply.
Compare the distance from each message bubble to its action row.
S6.18.where: Chat: the action row directly under a message, with Copy message under your message and Copy response under a reply

steps: Look at the message box at the bottom of the side panel.
Click in the box and type a few words.
Compare the space between the typed text and the box edge, and around the send control.
S6.19.where: Chat screen: the message box at the bottom of the side panel

S6.20.note: The chat message list uses a fixed 12px 10px padding in side_panel.ts with no width step found in the lines read, so this may not be met; whether Chrome allows the side panel edge to be dragged was not confirmed.
steps: Drag the left edge of the side panel to make it wider, then narrower.
Look at the margin between the content and the panel edge at each width.
Compare: the margin should change in steps with the width, not drift.
S6.20.where: Left and right margin of the chat and page content when the side panel is wider or narrower

S6.21.note: Recent chats is a tooltip and label on the clock icon, not visible text on the button.
steps: Click the clock icon in the chat header, labelled Recent chats.
Look at the rows in the list.
Compare: every row should have the same height, including rows with long titles.
S6.21.where: Click the Recent chats button (clock icon) in the chat header; the rows in the list are the sidebar history rows

steps: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header.
Look at the height of each menu item.
Compare: every item should have the same height and padding.
S6.22.where: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header; the menu items are Close tabs…, Extension settings, Shortcuts and Help

S6.23.note: The only dialog with its own padding found in the lines read is the media viewer (16px), so a single shared dialog padding was not confirmed.
steps: Click the clock icon in the chat header, labelled Recent chats.
Look at the space between the sheet edges and its heading, search box and list.
Compare the inner padding with the menu or other sheets you open.
S6.23.where: Click the Recent chats button (clock icon) in the chat header; the Recent chats sheet is the dialog

S6.24.note: Form spacing is set in apps/extension/src/options.ts; only the Appearance form was checked here.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button, then click Extension settings.
In the Options page, click Options in the left list.
Look at the Theme label, the select beneath it and the spacing between this row and the next form row.
Compare: label-to-input and field-to-field spacing should match across the form rows.
S6.24.where: More (⋮) > Extension settings > Options page, left list Options, Appearance section, Theme field

S6.25.note: The More (⋮) control is a text glyph, not an icon from the icon set.
steps: Look at the clock icon in the chat header and other icon buttons in the panel.
Compare their size and line weight with each other.
Compare: icons should come from one family with the same stroke and size.
S6.25.where: Icons in the chat header, for example the clock icon for Recent chats

S6.26.note: The code defines four fixed control heights, but no single screen shows all four at once, so the tester must compare several screens.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header.
Click "Shortcuts" to open the settings page.
Find the "Schedules" heading and look at "New schedule" and the other buttons beside it.
Compare their heights and padding with the side panel buttons, and check they come from a few fixed sizes.
S6.26.where: Effect is seen on the buttons in More (⋮) > Shortcuts > Schedules, for example "New schedule". Button sizes are set in apps/extension/src/side_panel.css (--control-sm 30px, --control-md 32px, --control-lg 34px, --control-touch 44px).

S6.27.note: Radius values come from the shared corner variables (for example var(--corner-control)); the tester only sees the result, not the scale itself.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header.
Click "Shortcuts".
Look at the corners of "New schedule" and the fields in the schedule form after clicking it.
Compare the corner curves across buttons, inputs and cards.
S6.27.where: Effect is seen on rounded corners of buttons and inputs, for example "New schedule" under More (⋮) > Shortcuts > Schedules.

S6.28.note: The exact text of the model button was not found in the code I read, so the tester must find it by its position in the header; the shadow rule is in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts.
steps: Open the side panel and open the model menu from the model button in the header.
Look at the shadow under the open menu.
Compare it with the shadow on the schedule form dialog or menus opened from More (⋮).
S6.28.where: Effect is seen on floating menus such as the side panel model menu, which uses the elevation shadow.

S6.29.needs: a conversation with an image in a reply, for the image-viewer step
S6.29.note: The layer numbers are in apps/extension/src/side_panel.css and apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts; the tester sees only the stacking result.
steps: Open the side panel and open a floating menu, such as the model menu from the header.
Scroll the chat behind the open menu.
Check that the menu stays above the chat text and buttons, and that a full-screen image viewer (opened from an image in a reply) covers the whole panel.
S6.29.where: Effect is seen when a floating menu or overlay covers page content in the side panel.

S6.30.note: Durations are named variables such as --duration-instant and --duration-spin in apps/extension/src/side_panel.css.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header.
Click "Shortcuts" and find "New schedule".
Move the pointer on and off "New schedule" and watch the colour and border change.
Open a menu and check the open motion is short and smooth, not slow or bouncy.
S6.30.where: Effect is seen as fades and slides on hover and when menus open, for example on "New schedule" under More (⋮) > Shortcuts > Schedules.

S6.31.needs: a Mac or another computer where the reduce-motion setting can be changed
S6.31.note: The code reads the operating system setting only; there is no in-app switch for reduced motion, and the loading indicator name was not confirmed.
steps: Turn on the reduce-motion setting in the operating system (find it under Accessibility in System Settings on a Mac; this path is not in the code).
Open the side panel and send a message, then watch the loading indicator while the reply is being made.
Open More (⋮) > Shortcuts and check that the page moves to a section without a long smooth scroll.
S6.31.where: Effect is seen when the operating system's reduce-motion setting is on: the code stops looping and travelling animations and turns smooth scrolling off. The macOS menu path is not in the code.

S6.32.needs: none (to test "System", change the computer's appearance in System Settings)
S6.32.note: The three choices are System, Light and Dark in apps/extension/src/features/appearance/themePreference.ts; the code does not confirm that code blocks change colour, so check that by eye.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button in the side panel header.
Click "Extension settings".
Click "Options" in the left list.
Under "Appearance", open the "Theme" menu and choose "Light", then "Dark", then "System".
Look at the side panel and the settings page: they should switch colours each time, and "System" should follow the computer's light or dark setting.
S6.32.where: More (⋮) > Extension settings > Options > Appearance > Theme (choose System, Light or Dark)

S6.33.needs: a Windows computer with High Contrast available; a Mac tester cannot trigger this
S6.33.note: Searched for 'high contrast' and 'prefers-contrast' in apps/extension/src; the only match is the forced-colors rule in apps/extension/src/tokens.ts and apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts. No in-app high-contrast option exists.
steps: On Windows, turn on High Contrast in the system settings (the Windows path is not in the code).
Open the side panel and then More (⋮) > Extension settings.
Check that text, borders and the focus outline use the system high-contrast colours.
S6.33.where: Only the Windows High Contrast mode is handled (CSS forced-colors). No in-app control was found, and the code does not respond to prefers-contrast.

S6.34.note: The state rules are in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts; whether "Create schedule" is disabled when empty was not checked in the code.
steps: Click the More (⋮) button and then "Extension settings", then "Options".
Move the pointer over a button in the left list and watch its hover state.
Press Tab to move focus and check the visible focus outline.
Press and hold a button with the mouse and check its pressed state; look for disabled buttons, such as "Create schedule" while the form is empty, and check they look different.
S6.34.where: Effect is seen on the buttons and the left list in More (⋮) > Extension settings > Options.

S6.35.note: Icon sizes are declared in apps/extension/manifest.json (16, 32, 48, 128); the brand mark on the Options page is apps/extension/icons/icon32.png and the empty-state mark is apps/extension/src/assets or icons/agi-symbol.png as loaded in apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts.
steps: Open Chrome and find the "AGI Extension" icon in the toolbar; if it is hidden, open the extensions menu (the puzzle-piece icon) and check its listing.
Open chrome://extensions and look at the "AGI Extension" icon at its large size.
Open the side panel, click More (⋮) > "Extension settings", and look at the brand mark and the name "AGI Extension" at the top left.
Open an empty side panel with no conversation and check the large centred logo mark.
S6.35.where: Chrome toolbar: the "AGI Extension" icon. Inside the app: More (⋮) > Extension settings, then the brand mark and name at the top left of the Options page.
